what_it_does: When a chip is manufactured, factories run 'structural tests' — they feed known signals into the chip and check whether the outputs match a model of expected good behavior, flagging chips that deviate as defective. At the smallest modern transistor sizes, however, the real physical defects that occur during fabrication are increasingly strange and subtle, and the standard models do not describe them well — so some bad chips slip through undetected. This invited paper proposes a new testing philosophy called Device-Aware Test (DAT), which goes beyond fixed structural test patterns by incorporating detailed knowledge of how specific device technologies actually behave (for example, how a particular transistor leaks current or degrades under stress) to expose those 'unmodeled' defects. The abstract describes the motivation and direction rather than a finished algorithm, so the exact mechanisms remain to be seen in the full paper.
